idle: 1994. Sixty-one goals. Look it up. It's in the window.
You know what we did in 1994? We WON.
Second period's a scam. Nobody needs a second period.
good_ice: Ice like this, I'd have scored seventy.
bad_ice: This ice is a crime. In '94 we'd have walked out.
Who flooded this, a garden hose?
wet_ice: Wet ice! My kid can't wire it on wet ice!
goal: THAT'S IT! THAT'S A SAUCIER GOAL!
Shoot it like that every time!
cold: Cold? This is nothing. 1994 we played outdoors. Once. It was cold.
long_line: I've told three stories in this line. Move it!
bored: Did I tell you about goal number 40? Backhand. From the boards.
greet_owner: {owner}! Did I ever tell you about 1994?
Hey, owner! Front row's mine, right?
leaving_angry: They'd never have done that in 1994. NEVER.

minor_hockey: SHOOT! MASON, SHOOT! Why isn't he shooting?
PASS IT! No! SHOOT IT! Okay that worked.
tournament: This is a big one. Sixty-one goals big.
Get him on the power play! Somebody! Anybody!
beer_league: Moose Knuckles! Same team as '94! Mostly the same knees!
I'm gassed. It's the second period. Of course I'm gassed.
senior_hockey: I'd have made the Kings. I'd have. Knee went in '96.

first.say: Rick Saucier. Sauce. Sixty-one goals, 1994, Millbrook Midget AA. You've seen the photo in my window. Everybody's seen the photo.

options.text: Sixty-one! Tell me about it.
I think I've heard about the tooth, actually.
Nice to meet you, Sauce.
I'll make it right, Sauce.
Maybe it's not all the rink's fault, Rick.

say: SHOOT! SHOOT IT! Sorry. Hi. Mason's on. SHOOT!
Did you see that? He passed! Why is he passing? I never passed!

options.text: Maybe let the coach coach, Rick.
He's playing great. Better than you at twelve, I bet.
I'll leave you to it.

minor_quiet.say: The coach. Right. The coach who 'develops'. You know who developed me? Nobody! And I scored sixty-one!

options.text: He can hear you from the bench, you know.

do.note: Told Sauce his son can hear him from the bench.

options.text: Remember, Rick. He can hear you.
Fair enough.

say: Moose Knuckles tonight. Same team as 1994. Same jerseys. Different knees.
I'm good for one period. Then it's all heart.

options.text: Save some legs for the second.
Any stories before the game?

say: {owner}! My buddy! Front row, glass, just like I like it.
Hey, it's my favourite rink owner! Story?

options.text: Hey, Sauce.

say: What's up? Quick, I've got a story loaded.
Sauce is here. You can relax now.
You know what this rink needs? More 1994.

options.text: Tell me a 1994 story.
How's Mason doing?
What's the deal with you and Dr. Haverkamp?
What do you think of the rink?
About Mason and the power play...
You called about Mason's ice time again.
See you on the ice, Sauce.
Gotta run, Sauce.

say: Story 3 of 61. 1994. I had hair. Look at the window photo. Hair, {owner}.
Story 7 of 61. 1994, Kessler, triple overtime. I scored with half a stick. The blade was in the corner.
Story 12 of 61. Sainte-Odile, 1994. Father Gagnon's nephew in net. I scored and he crossed himself. True story.
Story 23 of 61. The bus broke down at Carrick Junction. We pushed it. Then I scored four.
Story 31 of 61. August 1994, Ronnie brings the Cup home and I touched it. With this hand. Spiritually I haven't washed it.
Story 44 of 61. My coach said 'Ricky, you're going places.' I went to Harlow Falls. For a tractor show. Still counts.
Story 52 of 61. Goal number sixty. Wrist shot, top shelf. The goalie still sends me a Christmas card. It says 'stop telling it.'
Story 61 of 61. Goal sixty-one. Valley final. I don't even remember it. Everyone else does. Isn't that funny?

options.text: Another one.
Great story, Sauce.
You've told me that one.

mason.say: Kid's a natural. Better than me. Hands like... well, like mine. I just want him to have what I had. Sixty-one. A banner. People remembering.

options.text: Does he still have fun out there?
He'll get there.

mason_tender.say: ...He used to sing in the car. On the way TO games. Some song from a cartoon. He stopped last year. I don't know when. Anyway! Where was I? 1994!

options.text: Maybe ask him about the song.

do.note: Sauce mentioned that Mason used to sing in the car.

options.text: Right. 1994.

lyle.say: Haverkamp. That man sent me a bill for my own tooth. A Molars stick took it! Their stick! And now they wave toothbrushes at me in the handshake line.

options.text: You could just pay the bill, Rick.
It is a good toothbrush, I hear.
But it's settled now. Do you use the toothbrush?

rink.say: This place? Where I scored half of sixty-one? It's sacred. Also the glass is filthy. Front row deserves clean glass.

options.text: And the ice now? Better?
I'll get the glass cleaned.

rink_ice.say: Better than 1994, and I don't say that. I never say that. Write down that I said that.

options.text: Writing it down.

coach.say: Power play. First line. And the paper. That's all I'm asking. He's the best one out there, Coach.

options.text: He plays where he's ready. Not where you yell.
Rick, does he still have fun out there?
Mason told me he'd like a bit less pressure.
Did you ask him about the song?

coach_firm.say: Ready? I was ready at nine! ...Fine. FINE. But if he scores sixty-one for somebody else, that's on you.

options.text: I'll take that bet.

coach_song.say: I did. He sang it. In the car. On the way home, even. We lost 4-1 and he sang. I didn't say anything about the game. Not one word. That's a record.

options.text: That's the best record you've got, Sauce.

gm.say: He's a prospect, right? A real prospect? Just tell me he's on your list. In pen. Not pencil. Old Pete uses pencil. I hate the pencil.

options.text: He's on the list. In pencil, like everybody.
He's twelve, Rick. Let him be twelve.

player.say: You're on the Flood Crew? Ha! Moose Knuckles will eat you alive. For a period. Then we're tired. But for a period!

options.text: I'll wait for the second period, then.
